tasks.short: Take and clarify questions, look up current evidence, advise physicians, educators and researchers, write the advice note and file it for reuse.

steps.what: Medical scientist takes and clarifies questions from physicians and researchers
Medical scientist looks up current evidence on the question

loop.input: The clarified question and papers found in the library's licensed databases; no patient data.
loop.output: A short evidence summary with a citation per statement.
loop.check: Code keeps only citations that resolve to a DOI or database ID; each summary statement must match what the cited paper reports, including the population, dose and limits, or it is dropped; unclear statements go to the scientist, who reads each cited paper before using it.
loop.stop: One summary per question; no resolvable citations means the scientist searches by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions cross physics, biology and chemistry; keyword search returns too much to read.

steps.what: Medical scientist consults with and advises physicians, educators and researchers
Medical scientist writes the advice note on medical applications
Medical scientist files the advice note for reuse

tasks.design: A bounded step summarises evidence for the clarified question from the library's licensed databases, keeping only citations that resolve; the scientist reads every cited paper. Advice notes are filed with tags in the department's document space ({DOCS}) so earlier advice can be found. Clarifying, advising and writing the advice stay with the scientist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each question started with a fresh literature search.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models can extract and summarise data from papers with high accuracy in studies.
tasks.still_hard: Generated citations can be invented; every one must resolve and be read.
tasks.human_edge: Translating a physics finding into what it means for one patient group.
tasks.altitude: The scientist checks an evidence summary instead of building it.

reach.learn: Whether an advice archive cuts repeat questions.

evidence.claim: In a study of 10 trials and 160 data elements, a language model extracted data with 96.3% accuracy; 4 of 6 errors were missed items.
GPT-3.5 fabricated 55% and GPT-4 18% of 636 generated citations.
Health data are special category data, so no patient data go into the step.

assumptions: Boundary: from the request to the advice archive; acting on the advice is outside.
Input contract: questions from physicians, educators and researchers; papers from the hospital library's databases; fallback is searching by hand.

Clarifying, advising, writing and filing do not change; tagging notes for reuse is new work counted once in new work. Looking up evidence keeps 60 because the scientist reads every cited paper; only searching and screening go.
No patient data go into the evidence step.
research_questions: How often does the summary miss a key paper?

already_counted.description: Medical scientist reads each cited paper.

incremental.description: Medical scientist tags advice notes for reuse.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the licensed databases cover only half of the questions, so the rest are searched by hand and s2 keeps 80 (5.5); high: the evidence step covers most questions and s2 keeps 60 (11.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The medical scientist keeps advising and judgement; starting every search from scratch shrinks.
role.ambitious_version: A scientist whose earlier advice is easy to find and build on.
